'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russo-Ukrainian War]]
**[[2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis]]
***[[Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis]]
****[[Vladimir Putin]] claims that a "[[genocide]]" is occurring in Eastern Ukraine. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/putin-says-russia-does-not-want-war-calls-donbass-genocide-2022-02-15/ (Reuters)]
****The [[State Duma]] of [[Russia]] passes a bill to officially recognise the self-proclaimed [[Donetsk People's Republic]] and [[Luhansk People's Republic]] in [[Eastern Ukraine]] as independent states. The bill has been sent to [[President of Russia|President]] Vladimir Putin for final approval. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/europe/20220215/ab6821835bf8414189ae114cf188b1b1/c.html (Xinhuanet)] [https://www.dw.com/en/russian-duma-asks-putin-to-recognize-ukrainian-regions-as-independent/a-60783596 (Deutsche Welle)]
***[[President of Russia|Russian President]] [[Vladimir Putin]] says that diplomatic talks will continue. Russia also announces that troops will be partially pulled out from the border but that exercises will continue. [https://www.wsj.com/amp/articles/russia-says-some-troops-pulling-back-from-ukraine-border-but-exercises-continue-11644920006 (''Wall Street Journal'')] [https://truthout.org/video/russia-says-it-pulled-back-some-troops-from-ukraine-as-talks-continue/?amp (Truthout.org)]
***Several Ukrainian websites, including the [[Ministry of Defence of Ukraine]], [[Privatbank]], and [[Oschadbank]] are affected by [[cyberattack]]s. [https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/russia-ukraine-financial-defense-sites-under-attack-by-hackers/ (CBS News)]
***The U.S. and its [[NATO]] allies in [[Europe]] say that they are ready to retaliate against [[Cyberwarfare by Russia|Russian cyberwarfare]] on Ukraine depending on the severity of the attacks. [https://www.reuters.com/world/us-allies-ready-retaliate-russian-cyberattacks-say-officials-2022-02-15/ (Reuters)]
**[[War in Donbas]]
***The [[Luhansk People's Republic]] says that a [[Russian separatist forces in Donbas|service member]] has been killed on the frontline by a [[Armed Forces of Ukraine|Ukrainian military]] [[sniper]], according to its office at the [[Joint Centre of Control and Coordination]]. [https://www.urdupoint.com/en/world/lpr-says-its-servicemen-killed-in-donbas-afte-1470701.html (Urdu Point)]
***An attempted terrorist attack on a memorial rally in the city of [[Luhansk]] is reportedly stopped. [[Mass media in Russia|Russian media]] blames the [[Ministry of Defence (Ukraine)|Ukrainian Defence Ministry]] and "special services" of being involved in the attack. A video shows an [[improvised explosive device]] being discovered inside a garbage can. [https://www.jpost.com/breaking-news/article-696579 (''The Jerusalem Post'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[Capsizing of the Villa de Pitanxo|Capsizing of the ''Villa de Pitanxo'']]
**A [[Spain|Spanish]]-owned [[fishing trawler]], ''Villa de Pitanxo'', sinks off the coast of [[Newfoundland and Labrador]], [[Canada]], killing 10 crew members and leaving 11 others missing. A [[search and rescue]] operation is underway. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-us-canada-60392368 (BBC News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]]
****[[Indonesia]] reports a record 57,049 new [[COVID-19]] cases in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 4.9 million. [https://nasional.kompas.com/read/2022/02/15/17345961/update-15-februari-bertambah-26747-kasus-sembuh-covid-19-jadi-4349848 (''Kompas'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
****[[Japan]] reports a record 236  deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours. Meanwhile, the number of cumulative COVID-19 cases surpasses four million. [https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2022/02/15/national/covid-cases-february-15/ (''The Japan Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]]
****[[South Korea]] reports a record 57,177 new [[COVID-19]] cases in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 1.46 million. [http://www.koreaherald.com/view.php?ud=20220215000641 (''The Korea Herald'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Vietnam]]
****[[Vietnam]] lifts its COVID-19-related curbs on international passenger flights with no limitation on the number of flights in order to restore the travel to pre-pandemic level. [https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2022/2/14/vietnam-to-end-covid-curbs-on-international-flights (Al-Jazeera)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Canada convoy protest]]
**[[2022 alleged plot to kill Coutts RCMP officers]]
***Four men are arrested on suspicion of plotting to murder officers with the [[Royal Canadian Mounted Police]]. The arrests occurred during a protest blockading the Canada–U.S. border near [[Coutts, Alberta]]. [https://www.theglobeandmail.com/canada/alberta/article-rcmp-charge-four-men-with-plotting-to-murder-officers-in-connection/ (''The Globe and Mail'')]
**A number of protestors at Coutts have dispersed after an RCMP raid on a "smaller group within the larger protest" resulted in the seizure of weapons, ammunition, and body armour and the arrests of 13 people on Monday. [https://www.ctvnews.ca/canada/protesters-clear-coutts-alta-highway-after-weapons-seized-emergencies-act-invoked-1.5781971 (CTV News)]
**Chief of police of the [[Ottawa Police Service]] [[Peter Sloly]] resigns amid criticism of his handling of the protests. [https://ottawa.ctvnews.ca/ottawa-police-chief-peter-sloly-resigns-1.5782036 (CTV News Ottawa)]
*[[Sandy Hook Elementary School shooting]]
**Families of nine victims of the 2012 [[Sandy Hook Elementary School shooting]] reach a $73 million settlement with [[Remington Arms]], according to their attorney, Josh Koskoff.[https://www.cnn.com/2022/02/15/us/sandy-hook-shooting-settlement-with-remington (CNN)]
*Former [[President of Honduras|Honduran President]] [[Juan Orlando Hernández]] is arrested in [[Tegucigalpa]] after the U.S. requested his extradition on charges of drug trafficking. [https://www.efe.com/efe/espana/mundo/el-expresidente-hondureno-hernandez-es-capturado-tras-la-peticion-de-ee-uu-por-narcotrafico/10001-4740520 (EFE)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2022 United States elections]]
**[[2022 Louisville mayoral election]]
***In [[Louisville, Kentucky]], council candidate Quintez Brown is charged with attempted murder, a day after he allegedly opened fire on mayoral candidate Craig Greenberg in his campaign office, narrowly missing him.  [https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/council-candidate-accused-of-trying-to-kill-would-be-mayor/2022/02/15/ef6b9d3c-8e76-11ec-8ddd-52136988d263_story.html (AP via ''The Washington Post'')]
